mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates labor market stress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity accelerates.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the GDP declines over two consecutive quarters, the hypothesis is rejected.
